contract: PYAPIFIX2-01 — the venue-transient error body on the LIVE key-connect route (POST /api/validate-key) and its dead-route sibling (POST /api/verify-strategy). Every case below is the EXACT wire body the Python service emits: a FLAT object whose top-level `detail` is a SCALAR string, plus a machine `code` and a boolean `recoverable`. The scalar `detail` is the load-bearing half: src/lib/analytics-client.ts:174-181 does `error.detail ?? "Analytics service error"` and hands the result to `new AnalyticsUpstreamError(message, status)`, and src/lib/wizardErrors.ts:936-1035's `classifyKeyValidationError` is a SUBSTRING CASCADE over that message. If `detail` ever became an object the message would stringify to "[object Object]", every branch would miss, and RATE_LIMITED / PROBE_FAILED / DDOS_PROTECTION would regress from correct classification to UNKNOWN/500.
notes: COMMITTED, never generated. The `python` (ci.yml) and `frontend-test` (ci.yml) jobs are siblings with no `needs:` edge, so a file one job writes is invisible to the other. The Python consumer asserts these bodies equal what the REAL route emits through the REAL main.app exception-handler stack. The TypeScript consumer is a 140.3 obligation (ledger row TS-35): a `WizardErrorCode` branch that reads `body.code` instead of substring-matching `body.detail`, bound to THIS file so it never re-derives the case table. Neither consumer may derive its expectations from the module under test — every value here is a literal, and the Python test carries the same literals typed independently in the test file so the two are COMPARED, never sourced from one another. Synthetic values only; no credentials, no tenant data.
invariants: status is 424 at all seven sites — remapped from 400 by 140.3-06 (ledger row TS-32). 424 is CALLER'S EXCHANGE in analytics-service/docs/STATUS_CONTRACT.md §5: the third party THE CALLER NAMED is at fault. A 400 accused the caller of sending a malformed request on every one of these seven arms, which was false at all of them — the venue failed, not the user. The remap is BODY-NEUTRAL (main.py's handler serialises {detail, code, recoverable} independent of status, and the class guard already admitted any 400 <= status < 500), so every `body` object below is byte-identical to what shipped before it. The row's stated BLOCKED-BY: TS-05 named the WRONG row (CONTEXT correction C-4); the real blocker was TS-35, which landed in 140.3-05 and made `classifyKeyValidationError` read `body.code` before sniffing the message. Breaker-safe by construction: 424 is a 4xx, and src/lib/seam-discriminator.ts classifies it caller-exchange / counts:false / breakerKey:null, so a venue outage cannot open OUR breaker. NOTE: this FLAT shape carries no `dependency` key, unlike the nested `service_error(424, …)` form whose `_validate` arm REQUIRES a venue slug there — the two 424 shapes are distinguishable and the venue vocabulary never collides with SERVICE_DEPENDENCIES.
body key set is EXACTLY {detail, code, recoverable} — no more, no fewer.
body.detail is a scalar JSON string, byte-identical to the copy shipped before this contract existed. A reword is a CROSS-LANGUAGE breaking change.

recoverable derives from membership in services/exchange.py's PERMANENT_VALIDATION_ERROR_CODES allow-list, computed in the ROUTER. Non-membership means 'not known to be permanent', which that constant's contract defines as retryable — so an UNKNOWN future code yields recoverable=true (fail-safe). On this route `recoverable` is a RENDER hint (whether to offer a retry affordance), never an automated-retry-loop input; if 140.3 wires it into an automated loop the polarity must be re-derived.
consumers: analytics-service/tests/test_validate_key_venue_transient.py — asserts each body equals a REAL full-stack TestClient(main.app) response at the site named by site_id
(owed, 140.3 / ledger row TS-35) a TypeScript parity test binding the wizard's body.code branch to these same bytes

sites.C1: analytics-service/routers/exchange.py — sFOX HTTP 429 arm inside `except SfoxApiError`
sites.C2: analytics-service/routers/exchange.py — sFOX 5xx / status==0 transport arm inside `except SfoxApiError`
sites.C3: analytics-service/routers/exchange.py — `except asyncio.TimeoutError` around the MT5 RPyC probe
sites.C5: analytics-service/routers/exchange.py — the `classify_mt5_login_error(e) == transient` arm inside `except Mt5ClientError`. 167-CREDTRUST plan 01 (S-27) narrowed this ONE arm's code/detail/recoverable away from the shared venue-transient vocabulary below, and 167 WR-01 narrowed it again to login-stage refusals only — it carries TWO cases, see each case's own note.
sites.C6: analytics-service/routers/exchange.py — `if result["error"]:` after `validate_key_permissions` on the ccxt path (POST /api/validate-key)
sites.C7: analytics-service/routers/portfolio.py — `if validation.get("error"):` after `validate_key_permissions` in `verify_strategy`. DEAD ROUTE: no TypeScript caller exists. Included for CLASS INTEGRITY only — a class closed at six of its seven sites re-opens the moment the seventh is revived.

cases.note: sFOX answered 429. A throttle is an UPSTREAM condition, never bad credentials.

body.detail: Exchange rate-limited the validation request. Wait a moment and try again — repeated failures may indicate a missing read scope.

cases.note: sFOX answered 5xx (or status==0 transport blip). Upstream/transport, never the user's key.

body.detail: Network error reaching the exchange. Check connectivity and try again.

cases.note: The MT5 RPyC probe timed out — a hung upstream bridge. The code matches what the copy already says (NETWORK); vocabulary reused, never re-minted.

body.detail: Network error reaching the exchange. Check connectivity and try again.

cases.note: A concurrent validate re-logged the shared MT5 terminal onto another account mid-probe — an infra/concurrency fault, explicitly 'never the user's key'.

body.detail: Network error reaching the exchange. Check connectivity and try again.

cases.note: A LOGIN-STAGE refusal (Mt5LoginRefusedError: the terminal received the credential and answered login() itself falsy) whose code is not one of the -10000..-10004 IPC-infrastructure codes or the success code 1, classified `transient` by classify_mt5_login_error (e.g. code 0 or -6 with text the classifier does not recognise, or a login-stage -10005). 167-CREDTRUST plan 01 (D-05, D-07, S-27) NARROWS this answer away from the shared NETWORK_UNAVAILABLE vocabulary: a sign-in was actually attempted and refused, which SIGN_IN_FAILED claims and the network detail does not. recoverable flips to false, deliberately diverging from every sibling MT5 arm's hardcoded true (D-08): a retry re-sends the SAME credential to a terminal that either refuses it again or, in the -10005 case, puts the modal login dialog a wrong password raises back up (D-08, D-17). 167 WR-01 / D-17: a login-stage -10000..-10004 or 1, an initialize() failure, or any post-login fault reaching the same arm keeps NETWORK_UNAVAILABLE — see mt5_post_login_client_error. The other six sites in this fixture are BYTE-UNCHANGED.

body.detail: The sign-in attempt did not complete, and the venue did not confirm the credential.

cases.note: 167 WR-01 — the SAME `except Mt5ClientError` arm, reached AFTER the sign-in was accepted: login() succeeded and a post-login read (here account_info) raised an IPC timeout. No sign-in failed, so this keeps the pre-167 answer byte-for-byte — NETWORK_UNAVAILABLE, recoverable true. A second CASE at C5, not a new site: the arm answers two ways depending on which stage failed.

body.detail: Network error reaching the exchange. Check connectivity and try again.

cases.note: ccxt.RateLimitExceeded. This code classifies CORRECTLY today (substring 'rate' -> KEY_RATE_LIMIT); the byte-identical detail is what guarantees zero regression.

body.detail: Exchange rate-limited the validation request. Wait a moment and try again — repeated failures may indicate a missing read scope.

cases.note: ccxt.DDoSProtection. Classifies to KEY_IP_ALLOWLIST today (wrong code, right flavour) via 'ip'+'allow'; the byte-identical detail keeps that unchanged.

body.detail: Exchange blocked the validation request at the edge (DDoS / WAF protection). Check region / IP allowlist.

cases.note: ⭐ THE HEADLINE CASE. ccxt.ExchangeNotAvailable — a Binance maintenance window during key-connect. This copy matches NO branch of the substring cascade, so it renders today as UNKNOWN/500 'something went wrong, our team has been notified' with no retry affordance (the DOGFOOD-3 dead end). The machine `code` + `recoverable:true` on the wire is the Python half of killing that; the render half is 140.3's (TS-35).

body.detail: Exchange is currently unavailable. Try again in a few minutes.

cases.note: ccxt.NetworkError. The copy contains 'Network' but the cascade branch tests 'timeout'/'etimedout' — a two-string near-miss, so this ALSO lands on UNKNOWN/500 today.

body.detail: Network error reaching the exchange. Check connectivity and try again.

cases.note: detect_permissions returned its fail-CLOSED default after a transient exception. Classifies correctly today ('could not verify' -> KEY_PROBE_FAILED); pinned so it stays correct.

body.detail: Could not verify the key's permission scopes — the permission probe failed. Try again in a moment.

cases.note: PERMANENT CONTROL. AUTH_FAILED is in PERMANENT_VALIDATION_ERROR_CODES, so recoverable MUST be false. Without this case `recoverable` is decorative — a field that is always true pins nothing. The code rides for EVERY verdict at C6/C7, permanent ones included: that is closing the site, not absorbing the separate permanent-half gap.

body.detail: Authentication failed. Check your API key and secret.

cases.note: FAIL-SAFE CONTROL, the other polarity. A code the router has never seen must still yield recoverable=true, because PERMANENT_VALIDATION_ERROR_CODES is an ALLOW-LIST OF PERMANENT: non-membership means 'not known to be permanent'. The harm asymmetry decides it — a wrong `true` costs one pointless user click on a dead credential; a wrong `false` is the UNKNOWN/500 dead end this whole phase exists to kill. The synthetic code is deliberately not a real vocabulary member.

body.detail: A synthetic verdict from a venue code this router has never seen.

cases.note: The dead-route sibling of the headline case. Same collapse, same producer (validate_key_permissions), different handler. Closed for CLASS INTEGRITY, not user impact.

body.detail: Exchange is currently unavailable. Try again in a few minutes.

cases.note: The permanent control at C7 too — the recoverable derivation must be the SAME rule at both collapse sites, not a rule that happens to hold at the one with traffic.
